primary_issue: The shatter event has almost no readable impact: the brick/impact moment is unclear and there is little-to-no outward shard eruption or secondary collapse, so the core action described in the scene doesn’t land.
issues: CRITICAL: The main action beat (brick striking/punching through center of pane) is not clearly readable; the brick is tiny/indistinct and doesn’t convincingly interact with the glass.
CRITICAL: Shatter intensity is far too weak—no explosive outward burst of shards, no dense debris field, and no sense of force/speed.
HIGH: Remaining glass does not visibly crack and collapse from the frame edges after impact (missing the “attached glass collapses” beat).
HIGH: Environment does not read as a gritty derelict industrial warehouse; materials/props feel like a clean CG blockout (minimal grime, rust, wear, and industrial detail).
HIGH: Window/frame material reads closer to plain trim/wood than rusted steel; this breaks the intended look.
HIGH: Composition/camera places the window/action too small in frame; large empty wall dominates, reducing drama and readability.
MEDIUM: Lighting is not cinematic/moody enough for “night warehouse”; limited contrast/atmosphere and insufficient specular catches to make shards/cracks pop.
MEDIUM: Glass fracture pattern is simplistic/faint (missing dense radial + concentric cracking and micro-fragmentation around the impact core).
MEDIUM: Overall render has a low-fidelity CG/material feel (flat shading, surfaces too clean, limited roughness/texture breakup).
suggestions: (Outside current 13 shader params) Make the impact readable: increase brick size and place it clearly on a left-to-right trajectory through the pane; add motion blur on the brick and fastest shards.

(Outside current 13 shader params) Increase fracture/shard density dramatically (hundreds+ pieces), with a strong outward ballistic burst from the impact point and varied shard size/rotation; add a fragment “trail” following the brick.
(Outside current 13 shader params) Add a second-stage collapse for edge-attached glass (larger retained chunks near the frame that crack and drop after the initial burst).
Reframe the camera closer or zoom so the window + impact point dominate the shot (reduce dead wall space).
Improve shard readability via lighting: add a strong grazing/rim light to catch shard edges; add subtle volumetric haze/dust so light beams and debris read.

Script shader tweaks to avoid overly dark/tinted glass: Line 251 absorption Density 0.12 → ~0.02–0.05; Line 250 absorption Color (0.55, 0.95, 0.66, 1.0) → more neutral/slightly green (e.g., ~0.85,0.95,0.9) to keep glass clear.
Reduce “procedural pattern” dominance on glass: Line 220 wave Distortion 2.0 → ~0.5–1.0; Line 221 bump Strength 0.08 → ~0.02–0.05 (helps avoid plasticky/over-bumpy glass).
If emission is being used to ‘show’ glass, keep it subtle: Line 267 emission Strength → very low (or off) and rely on proper specular/rim lighting instead; emissive glass will look fake quickly.

Push gritty warehouse look (outside current params): rusted steel frame (roughness variation + corrosion), stained concrete, grime streaks, chipped paint, dusty props; add deeper interior set dressing visible through the window.
vision_assessment: The render shows a simple interior wall with a window opening and a warm wall-mounted light casting a broad shadow. A few basic props (boxes/barrel) sit near the wall. The window/glass break is only faintly indicated by a small set of crack-like streaks; there is no clear explosive shatter, no visible cloud of flying shards, and no obvious brick-punch-through moment. Overall it reads like an early blocking/previz pass rather than a gritty, cinematic warehouse shot with high-energy glass destruction.
